lead: The landscape of education is rapidly evolving, with debates surrounding technology use in classrooms, student protests over exam integrity, and initiatives to prepare unemployed youth for the job market through AI training.

stories.title: ‘Our children are less cognitively capable,’ says neuroscientist who wants to cut screen use in schools
stories.summary: Neuroscientist Jared Cooney Horvath argues that the increasing use of screens in education is detrimental to children's cognitive development. He highlights the need for a reevaluation of educational technology, suggesting that it may be undermining traditional learning methods. His insights come amidst growing concerns about the impact of digital tools on young learners.

stories.title: AI cheating, leaked papers and marking errors: how exam protests went global
stories.summary: Student unrest has erupted globally, particularly in Mexico and Portugal, where exam-related issues have sparked mass protests. In Mexico, nearly 60,000 students were forced to resit tests due to suspected cheating, while Portugal faced a crisis following a failed digitization of exam marking. These events highlight the pressures students face in a competitive job market.

stories.title: Unemployed young people to join AI boot camps to get job-ready
stories.summary: In an effort to combat youth unemployment, the UK government is launching AI boot camps aimed at equipping young people with skills for the job market. This initiative targets those not in education or employment, providing three weeks of training to help them harness AI technology. The program reflects a shift towards integrating technology into workforce readiness.
